heading: Key Sources
title: BCCNM - Using Artificial Intelligence in Practice
note: BCCNM has no AI-specific standard; this NP resource maps the standards that apply (privacy, consent, Indigenous cultural safety, conflict of interest, duty to provide care) to questions to ask before using AI
keywords: bccnm ai standard nurse practitioner accountability

heading: Key Sources
title: BC Ministry of Health - Responsible Artificial Intelligence Policy Framework
note: the Ministry's standards for AI used by the Ministry and BC health authorities: AI lifecycle, principles, risk management, informed consent, accountability and incident management; initial compliance expected by August 31, 2027
keywords: ministry of health ai policy framework health authorities governance

heading: Key Sources
title: CNPS - Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Legal Risk Management Considerations in Nursing Practice
note: the Canadian Nurses Protective Society on the legal risks of AI for nurses and NPs: reliability of output, bias, privacy and consent; the full article needs a CNPS beneficiary sign-in

heading: Nursing Regulators in Other Provinces
title: CRNA - Artificial Intelligence Practice Advice
note: Alberta guidance, not BC: the College of Registered Nurses of Alberta's advice for RNs and NPs using AI

heading: Nursing Regulators in Other Provinces
title: CNO - Artificial Intelligence in Nursing Practice
note: Ontario guidance, not BC: the College of Nurses of Ontario's AI learning tool (adapted with BCCNM's permission) and its FAQ on documenting with AI

heading: Physician-Focused Guidance
title: CPSBC - Ethical Principles for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
note: Physician-focused: the College of Physicians and Surgeons of BC's professional guideline, effective April 11, 2024
keywords: cpsbc college of physicians ethics ai

heading: Physician-Focused Guidance
title: CMPA - The Medico-Legal Lens on AI Use by Canadian Physicians
note: Physician-focused: CMPA paper on AI risk by type of tool, bias, the regulatory gaps and who is responsible for what

heading: Principles and Horizon Scans
title: Health Canada - Pan-Canadian AI for Health (AI4H) Guiding Principles
note: federal, provincial and territorial principles for responsible AI in health systems, including safety and oversight, accountability and transparency

heading: Principles and Horizon Scans
title: CDA-AMC - 2025 Watch List: Artificial Intelligence in Health Care
note: Canada's Drug Agency horizon scan of AI technologies in health care and the top issues they raise
keywords: cda-amc cadth horizon scan watch list

heading: Principles and Horizon Scans
title: WHO - Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health: Guidance on Large Multi-Modal Models
note: International source: World Health Organization guidance on generative AI in health care, its risks (false or biased output, automation bias) and recommendations for providers
